extracted.intended_audience: EPA rulewriters, agency scientists, environmental lawyers, and public commenters on the EPA residual risk/NESHAP rule for oil & gas
extracted.subtask_description: Public-comment/legal critique of EPA's Draft Residual Risk Assessment and related NESHAP/MACT rulemaking for oil and gas production, transmission, and storage, specifying scientific, procedural, and statutory deficiencies EPA must remedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterize HAP emissions (chemicals, volatilization, quantities, mixture effects)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must account for the types of chemicals used, volatilization potential, quantities of emissions, and potential for health impacts both individually and through exposures to a mixture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use available industry disclosure registries (e.g., FracFocus) and databases (e.g., TDEX). EPA's failure to characterize new/different types of HAP emissions from hydraulic fracturing (including new chemicals and methods) renders the risk analysis arbitrary and unlawful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address hydrogen sulfide (H2S) emissions and listing status
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must address health risk from hydrogen sulfide emissions and act on the pending petition to list H2S as a hazardous air pollutant under CAA §112.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: H2S has documented health effects and EPA has recognized its TRI reporting need; EPA therefore has sufficient toxicity data and legal obligation to include and evaluate H2S in this rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider community health data and local/agency studies
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must collect, consider and address available information about community health impacts and analyze this as part of its residual risk assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate findings from CDC/ATSDR, AOEC, PEHSU, state and local health departments (e.g., Garfield County), municipal studies (e.g., Town of Dish, Fort Worth), and community monitoring. These data (including elevated cancer/health complaints) are relevant and must be integrated into the risk analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess cancer/chronic risk at the maximum-exposed individual (fence line), not census block centroid
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's modeling understates cancer and chronic health risk by using census block centroids as exposure surrogates instead of assessing exposure at the facility fence line or other specific locations of residences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 112(f) requires analysis for the individual most exposed to emissions. Adjust receptor points to reflect the closest or most-exposed residences (SAB recommended considering specific locations). The HEM‑AERMOD system can and should be used to model fence-line/closest-residence exposures, as was done for acute risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include malfunctions, violations, and SSM events in risk analysis and quantify their likelihood
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must perform the risk analysis based on emissions that may occur during malfunctions and other violations (not just 'actual' or reported emissions), because such events increase HAP emissions and health risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use enforcement and malfunction history data and statistical/probability methods routinely used in MACT processes to quantify the likelihood and magnitude of exceedances. Do not treat emissions from noncompliance as zero. Consider that EPA's proposed 'affirmative defense' to civil penalties could reduce deterrence and increase occurrences of exceedances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate LDAR provisions and exemptions for their impact on HAP emissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Equipment leak provisions (LDAR) in the proposal carry over exemptions from earlier NSPS without evaluating their appropriateness for HAP regulation or their impact on hazardous air pollutant emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update LDAR to reflect best-performing sources, remove inappropriate exemptions, and analyze how exemptions affect HAP emissions and residual risk for communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use scientifically justified worst-case multipliers for acute exposure estimation and include MACT-allowable spikes
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's assumption that maximum 1-hour emissions are only 10 times the yearly average lacks rational explanation and likely underestimates acute exposure; EPA also failed to assess acute risk at MACT-allowable emission levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide scientific justification for any multiplier; consider higher multipliers or other worst-case approaches; include analysis of exposures if emissions occurred at MACT-allowable levels, since allowable levels may exceed estimated 'actual' emissions and produce acute spikes (e.g., for benzene).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess risk for all emitted HAPs, including those lacking reference values; use uncertainty factors or alternative data
rubrics_metrics.description: When EPA acknowledges emissions of HAPs but lacks reference values, it must not omit or assume zero risk; at minimum it must apply uncertainty factors or use available state screening levels or other scientific information to estimate risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document gaps and either perform qualitative assessments or apply conservative uncertainty factors until toxicity reference values are available. Example: Michigan ITSL for 2,2,4-trimethylpentane could inform screening; for benzene use the high end of IRIS ranges. Section 112 requires addressing all emitted HAPs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use up-to-date IRIS/toxicity information or adopt protective assumptions and set a re-review deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Because IRIS reviews for important pollutants (e.g., naphthalene, formaldehyde) are delayed or outdated, EPA must use the best available science from ongoing reviews or apply more protective assumptions and set a regulatory deadline to revisit the residual risk analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use interim best-available information where IRIS is incomplete; if EPA must wait for reassessments, adopt more protective values in the meantime. Commit to reperforming the residual risk rulemaking within a set timeframe (commenters recommend no later than eight years) once new reference values are available. Cite GAO and CPR findings on IRIS delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perform full multipathway risk assessments including child-specific scenarios, updated exposure factors, and urban/rural contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's multipathway analysis was only a screening and did not include full multipathway assessments (including child exposure scenarios) even where screening indicated POM emissions exceeded the 'de minimis' threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct multipathway assessments for urban and rural residential scenarios, include children's unique exposures (hand-to-mouth and object-to-mouth behavior), and use up-to-date Exposure Factors Handbook values (2011 EFH and 2008 Child-Specific EFH). Account for soil contamination, bioaccumulation, and behaviors that elevate child exposures (e.g., toddler contact frequencies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include contaminants beyond the PB-HAP list in multipathway analysis (do not limit to bioaccumulative list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Restricting multipathway analysis to only contaminants identified as persistent and bioaccumulative (PB-HAPs) is not supported by EPA guidance and underestimates multipathway risk from other persistent contaminants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow 2003 Guidance which indicates multipathway risk assessment may be appropriate when persistent pollutants that may bioaccumulate are present, but does not limit assessments to a fixed PB-HAP list. Evaluate persistent HAPs (e.g., beryllium, arsenic) that can deposit to soil and present exposure risks, particularly to children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate multipathway risk into overall risk characterization (additive with inhalation risk)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where multipathway analysis indicates more than 'de minimis' risk (e.g., POM), EPA must add multipathway risk to inhalation risk in its overall risk assessment rather than ignoring or isolating it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If screening shows multipathway risk above thresholds, perform full analysis and include those results in total risk metrics for facilities and most-exposed individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide transparent documentation of data gaps, methods, and rationale to allow meaningful public comment
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's charts and tables have many gaps without explanation of whether gaps indicate missing reference values; EPA has failed to provide a transparent discussion that would inform public comment as required by 42 U.S.C. § 7607(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify each missing reference/value, explain why it is missing, state what alternative data or methods were considered and why, and disclose how uncertainties were factored into the risk characterization so the public can meaningfully comment.
